I do not know what a party is, but I know that I am not part of it. I am Hoot, and I am alone.

Speed of light? I have never heard that word. The fastest thing I know is the blink of my eye, and that is only when I am startled by a sudden rustle in the leaves. The light from the moon comes to me in a moment, and the light from the barn is slower, because it is not so bright. I do not think about speed. I think about the hunt, the call of my mate, and the cold wind in the hollow.

I have seen them once, in the summer, when the sun was hot and the air was still. They were all over the hive, and they made a sound like a thousand wasps. I did not touch them, because I do not like the way they smell.

Owls are not like the other birds. They do not sing, they do not call to their mates with the same kind of voice. They have a different way of speaking, a low, soft sound, like a whisper.
